title: Formula for the canonical transpose of the universe-lifted transition
statement:
theorem finitePerfectAdicLiftedTransition_canonical_transpose_formula
    {A : Type t} [CommRing A] {d : AdicCoefficientDatum A}
    (T : FinitePerfectAdicAlgebraTower d) (n : ℕ) :
    let q : ULift.{t + 1} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1 + 1)) →+*
        ULift.{t + 1} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1)) :=
      RingHom.ulift (Ideal.Quotient.factorPowSucc d.ideal (n + 1))
    letI : (normalizationModuleRestrict q).IsRightAdjoint :=
      ModuleCat.derivedRestrictScalars_isRightAdjoint.{t + 1, 0} q
    let adj := Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (normalizationModuleRestrict q)
    ∃ e : (normalizationModuleRestrict q).leftAdjoint.obj
          ((finitePerfectAdicAlgebraLift _).obj (T.level (n + 1))) ≅
        (finitePerfectAdicAlgebraLift _).obj
          ((T.stepExtension n).obj (T.level (n + 1))),
      (adj.homEquiv _ _).symm (finitePerfectAdicLiftedTransition T n) =
        e.hom ≫ (finitePerfectAdicAlgebraLift _).map
          ((T.stepAdjunction n).homEquiv _ _ |>.symm (T.transition n))

source.place: Tags 06YY and 09C6, mate calculation for the universe-lifted transition

proof.text: For a homomorphism q:B→D, define the comparison from the canonical lifted scalar extension of the coefficient lift of P to the coefficient lift of the canonical small scalar extension of P as the transpose of the lifted small adjunction unit followed by finitePerfectAdicAlgebraLiftRestrict.inv. Its naturality follows by applying the large Hom equivalence, then using naturality of the small unit and the exact restriction comparison.

On a cochain representative, postcompose this mate with the lifted small scalar-extension representative and its exact localization factor. Applying the large Hom equivalence and the exact-square factorization identity reduces the resulting square to the ordinary unit identity for the inverse lifted tensor comparison. Degreewise this identity sends up(m) to up(1 tensor m) on both sides, so follows by extensionality and reflexivity. The ordinary tensor comparison is the existing natural ULift tensor equivalence.

Choose a small K-flat resolution that remains K-flat after coefficient-universe lift. The small and large canonical representative maps are then isomorphisms. The cochain comparison square expresses the mate followed by isomorphisms as an isomorphism, so the mate itself is invertible at this resolution. Its naturality transports invertibility along the resolution augmentation and the canonical representative isomorphism to every small derived object. No boundedness or perfectness hypothesis is needed.

At T.level(n+1), compose the resulting mate isomorphism with the coefficient lift of leftAdjointUniq from the canonical small scalar extension to T.stepExtension(n). Apply the canonical large Hom equivalence to the required formula. Naturality of the restriction comparison moves the lifted supplied transpose to the small side; the unit equation for leftAdjointUniq changes the canonical unit into T.stepAdjunction(n).unit. The small Hom-equivalence inverse identity then gives exactly T.transition(n), which is the defining lifted transition.

proof_origin.place: Tags 06YY and 07A6; more-algebra.tex Tag 06Y4. Agent-written coefficient-universe mate calculation using existing K-flat resolutions and exact-localization factorization.
